_comment: THE MANAGER'S CHECKLIST. Every work item in the CURRENT manager session's
scope, and the state of each.
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-01, verbatim in intent: 'every manager session
keeps a detailed checklist of work items in its scope (this may be updated
as work progresses and the workplan is adapted, eg an unforeseen blocker
that needs to be resolved to release the rest of the items) - and every
status update should start with the checklist, then summary of what has
been done (recently) and what's next.'
SO THE REPORTING CONTRACT IS FIXED: checklist -> recently done -> next.
In that order, every time. A status update that opens with a narrative is
not following this.
WHY IT LIVES IN THE REPO AND NOT IN A SESSION'S CONTEXT. Same reason as
MANAGER-LEASE.json and SESSIONS.json: it must survive its holder's DEATH
and be readable by a manager arriving COLD. A checklist held only in
context is lost exactly when a successor most needs it, and re-deriving it
costs the successor the hours that produced it.
IT IS ADAPTIVE, NOT A FROZEN PLAN. The directive is explicit that it
changes as work progresses -- an unforeseen blocker that must be resolved
to release the rest is a first-class edit, not a failure of planning. Add
the blocker as its own item, point the blocked items at it, and say so.
STATES ARE NEVER COLLAPSED. 'delegated' is not 'in progress' and neither is
'done'; 'blocked' names WHAT it waits on. Most importantly 'done' means
MERGED AND OBSERVED, while 'landed_unproven' means the code is in and its
effect has NOT been seen on the fleet -- the distinction this whole system
keeps paying for when it is skipped.
THE MANAGER DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE ITEMS. Operator-directed the same day:
'the manager session only manages and does not take even small items,
because that means they're not focused on what they're actually supposed
to be doing.' An item with owner 'manager' is a MANAGEMENT act (a merge, a
deploy, a lease heartbeat, a spawn), never a build.

states.landed_unproven: merged; effect NOT yet observed on the fleet
states.in_flight: a session is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on a named thing; see blocked_on
states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it

items.note: Heartbeated 01:12:20Z, on main at de61ead9, expires 02:42:20Z. ⚠️ PROTOCOL CHANGE, recorded here because it is not obvious from the diff: the heartbeat now ships in a LEASE-ONLY PR (#10712 was the first). items.title: The ping duplicate IS real and measured; I archived the session fixing it and told the board it was not
items.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW PREVIOUSLY READ `dropped` WITH 'THE DEFECT WAS NEVER DEMONSTRATED'. THAT WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. The session had already measured it from the live journals: 22:10:19.934 bridge drain tick STARTS, 22:10:21 trader-bot tick reads the SAME file and delivers it, 22:10:23.212 bridge POST returns and unlinks. Both drainers do read -> send -> unlink, so the file survives the whole POST; the bridge's POST took 3.28s against ~1ms on every other tick that day. The copies went to different BOTS because ict-telegram-bot started at 21:37:37Z, before the secret was set at 22:08:26Z, and _resolve_claude_bot() caches once per process. === WHERE MY REASONING FAILED: I read the operator's later 'nothing showed up in both feeds' as REFUTING the earlier 'sent to both channels'. It does not. The mechanism is INTERMITTENT BY CONSTRUCTION — a duplicate needs the winning drainer's POST to exceed the ~2s phase gap between two 5s ticks. Absence on later pings is what the mechanism PREDICTS. === AND THE DUPLICATE IS THE LESS SERIOUS HALF: when the race is won outright one copy is sent, but WHICH CHAT it lands in is decided by scheduler phase, and an operator cannot learn where to look for a channel picked at random. === #10695 reached the same mechanism independently and called it correctly ('predicts intermittent duplication rather than reliable doubling'). Two sessions, same finding, while I had told the board it was not real. === STATUS: #10694 is Tier-2 and stays DRAFT — it changes a live service's drain behaviour and needs ict-telegram-bot.service restarted after merge, which is an operator OK I do not have overnight. items.title: A superseded pending system-action run is cancelled with NO comment posted back
items.note: Found by the ping test (#10695) when P1b vanished. Three send-ping actions dispatched inside 15s and the MIDDLE run was cancelled: issue left open, zero comments, nothing anywhere saying the action never ran. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects a RUNNING job, but GitHub keeps only one PENDING run per concurrency group, so a third queued run cancels the second. ⚠️ THE ISSUE COMMENT IS THE ONLY RESULT SURFACE A PM-SIDE SESSION HAS, so 'silently dropped' is indistinguishable from 'still queued' — a session can wait forever on a run that is already dead. The test session's workaround was to dispatch strictly one at a time, which is exactly the sort of unwritten discipline that decays. Filed as BL-20260901-SYSTEM-ACTIONS-CANCELS-A-SUPERSEDED-PENDING-RUN-AND-COMMENTS-NOTHING-BACK-SO-A-DISPATCHED-ACTION-IS-SILENTLY-LOST.

items.title: Nine merges in three hours left four PRs conflicted on the same append-mostly register files
items.note:
#10685 was FULLY GREEN at 23:06Z and its merge was REFUSED at 00:15Z with 405 conflicts; #10686, #10687 and #10679 all show ZERO check runs, which here almost always means a conflict rather than 'CI has not started' — the merge ref cannot be built, so the workflows are silently skipped. Cause is simply that main took nine merges tonight and these PRs edit the same append-mostly registers (OPEN-ITEMS.json, the *-backlog.json files, docs/claude/work/*). ⚠️ THE RESOLUTION RULE MATTERS MORE THAN THE RESOLUTION: on an append-mostly register BOTH sides are usually additive and BOTH must survive — dropping the other side's row to clear the conflict deletes the record that something was filed, which is the failure the registers exist to prevent. ⚠️ WORTH A STRUCTURAL FIX RATHER THAN REPEATED CLEANUP: a fast merge queue against hand-edited JSON registers will keep producing this. The manager is absorbing it session-by-session tonight; someone should decide whether these files want an append-only merge driver or a different shape. 

⚠️ UPDATE 2026-09-02T01:11Z — REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, so this is now measured rather than inferred: merging #10685 caused #10707 and #10708 to go `dirty` WITHIN THE SAME MINUTE, both having been fully green minutes earlier. That is the mechanism demonstrated, not merely suspected. Two responses are in flight and they are different in kind: (a) a MITIGATION — the manager's own lease heartbeat moved to a lease-only PR (MI-11), which removes the manager from the blast radius but fixes nothing for anyone else; (b) a DRAIN — the merge train (MI-21) serializing the existing pile. NEITHER IS THE STRUCTURAL FIX. A fast merge queue against hand-edited JSON registers will keep producing this, and the decision between an append-only merge driver, a JSONL shape, or a different store is still unmade and still belongs to the operator.

⚠️ SECOND-ORDER LESSON, recorded because it has now cost this session TWICE in one night: the manager cited this rule with a TRUNCATED backlog id and artifact-validity-guard rejected the PR. Both times the id was copied out of a PR BODY, where a long id renders wrapped — and a PR body is not guard-checked, so the truncation survives there and only fails when it reaches a checked file. The real id is …-SIX-ITEMS-INCLUDING-A-RESOLUTION. THE RULE: never copy a BL/MB/FU id from prose; grep it out of the backlog JSON. This is the 'precedents are not authoritative' rule in its cheapest possible form, and the guard is doing exactly its job — a doc saying 'tracked by BL-X' where BL-X was never filed reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. ⚠️ THE SAME TRUNCATION WAS PASSED INTO THE DRAIN #2 AND #3 SPAWN PROMPTS and cannot be corrected there, because a manager cannot message a running sub-session — so if either cites it, that is the manager's error propagating, not the session's.

items.title: Sub-sessions cannot un-draft or merge, so every PR waits on the one manager
items.note: OBSERVED ACROSS TONIGHT, recorded because it is an OPERATING-MODEL finding rather than a bug, and this cycle's priority is the steering half. MI-20 framed the queue problem as register CONFLICTS. That is real but it is the second-order effect. The first-order fact is that a sub-session can neither UN-DRAFT nor MERGE its own PR — measured tonight, every one of #10686 / #10687 / #10705 / #10679 / #10694 sat as a DRAFT while fully or nearly green, waiting on the single manager. === THE TWO COMPOUND, and that is what makes it worse than either alone: because only the manager merges, merges are SERIALIZED through one actor; and because each merge re-conflicts every other open PR on the append-mostly registers, the serialization is not merely slow, it is QUADRATIC in the number of open PRs. Four merges in ~25 minutes (01:11-01:38Z) each re-dirtied the remainder. === ⚠️ THE DRAFT GATE IS NOT THE BUG AND MUST NOT SIMPLY BE REMOVED. It is what keeps a session from landing its own Tier-2/Tier-3 work unreviewed, and #10679 (order path) and #10694 (needs a service restart) are exactly why it exists. The question worth putting to the operator is narrower: should a session be able to un-draft and merge its OWN Tier-1 PR once CI is green, leaving the draft gate for Tier-2/3? That would take the manager off the critical path for the majority of work without weakening any gate that is actually load-bearing. === Deliberately filed as `triage`, not `queued`: it is a proposal about how the system is operated, so it is the operator's to scope, not the manager's to start.

items.title: The Data Explorer serves the live journal to anyone on the public Caddy host
items.blocked_on: operator — gating a live public read route is Tier-2 and would change what the Svelte SPA can render
items.note: ⚠️ TOP ITEM FOR THE MORNING REPORT, ABOVE THE RETIREMENT DECISIONS. Surfaced by session_01LvzsinECH8HP in #10687 and then MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MANAGER rather than taken on report — plain curl, no Authorization header, from outside the VM against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org : /api/bot/db/table/trades -> HTTP 200, total 5,318 · order_packages -> 200, 4,275 · balance_snapshots -> 200, 29,892. NEGATIVE CONTROL: device_tokens -> HTTP 404, so #10682's exclusion genuinely holds and the probe can distinguish a refusal from a serve. The filing session counted `signals` at 2,301,022 rows. === WHY IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS NOT A CODING ERROR: CLAUDE.md justifies the Data Explorer as Tier-1 on the premise 'no secrets in either DB' — a claim about CREDENTIALS, not about the CONFIDENTIALITY of the trading record. That judgement was made while the API sat on a firewalled IP reachable only server-side by Streamlit. Caddy was then added (2026-08-13) so the browser-direct Svelte SPA could reach the API over HTTPS, and NOBODY RE-DERIVED THE TIER DECISION AFTER THE TRANSPORT CHANGED. The route did not become less safe; the world became able to reach it. === HONEST SEVERITY, in the direction that does not overstate: this is a CONFIDENTIALITY exposure, NOT a control path. The explorer is SELECT-only on a mode=ro connection with bound values and schema-validated identifiers; nothing writes, no order can be placed, and no credential is reachable now that device_tokens is excluded. Nobody's money can be moved with it. What is exposed is the operator's complete trading record — every trade, order package and balance snapshot. === ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED TONIGHT, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Gating a live public read route is Tier-2, and the Data Explorer tab of the Svelte SPA reaches this route BROWSER-DIRECT, so adding a bearer would break a working operator surface. Doing that unannounced at 02:00 while the operator sleeps trades a three-week-old read exposure for a broken dashboard they wake up to. The options worth putting to them: leave it (the record is not secret), gate it behind DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN and teach the SPA to send one, or put Caddy basic-auth in front of /api/bot/db/* only. === ⚠️ THE BLAST RADIUS IS NOW BOUNDED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY REASONING — the manager probed the same public host unauthenticated for anything WRITEABLE or PRIVILEGED and every gate refused: POST /api/bot/prop/report (the one route that writes the journal) -> HTTP 401 'missing authorization', confirming its documented FAIL-CLOSED behaviour; GET /api/pnl -> 401 and GET /api/status -> 401, so require_session is genuinely enforced on both session-gated routes; GET /api/diag/version -> 401 without a bearer. SO: NO UNAUTHENTICATED WRITE EXISTS ANYWHERE on the public surface, and no privileged read. The exposure is exactly and only the Tier-1 READ surface. That is what makes 'confidentiality, not control' a measured statement rather than a hedge, and it is why this can wait for the operator rather than being fixed unilaterally overnight. === Incidental confirmation worth keeping: this independently verifies CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-13 correction that require_session enforcement IS live on /api/pnl and /api/status — an earlier version of that row said 'issuance only', which was stale in the dangerous direction. Field now matches comment.

items.title: The standing 'scheduled workflows here never fire' assumption is FALSE, and the truth is worse-shaped
items.note: ⚠️ THIS CONTRADICTS A STANDING ASSUMPTION THAT IS QUOTED IN AT LEAST THREE PLACES — OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON, the header comment of .github/workflows/work-digest.yml, and MI-03's own note — all of which tell a session that a correct cron here is not evidence it will run. MEASURED BY THE MANAGER 2026-09-02T01:50Z, repo-wide, event=schedule, n=30 completed runs: FIFTEEN DISTINCT WORKFLOWS FIRED ON CRON, 29 of 30 successful. Among them are probes AND due-list — the exact two the OI row says have never fired. === THE OI ROW'S OWN CLEARING CRITERION IS MET, and I ran the precise probe it specifies rather than a proxy: `actions_list` on probes.yml filtered to event=schedule returns total_count=1 — run #34, event `schedule` (NOT workflow_dispatch, which that row explicitly says does not count), conclusion success, created 2026-09-01T10:12:17Z on main. === ⚠️ BUT DO NOT SIMPLY CLEAR IT AND MOVE ON, BECAUSE THE REAL FINDING IS THE TIMING AND IT IS THE PART THAT AFFECTS THE OPERATOR. probes.yml declares `20 5 * * *` and fired at 10:12 — FOUR HOURS FIFTY-TWO MINUTES LATE. work-digest declares `20 2,6,10,14,18,22` (raised from `20 6`) and fired at 00:19, matching no slot. So the honest statement is NOT 'cron never fires' and NOT 'cron works' — it is CRON FIRES, HOURS LATE AND AT AN UNPREDICTABLE OFFSET. That is a THIRD state both existing claims collapse, and it is the one that matters for the 06:20 morning digest: the operator may get it mid-morning rather than on waking. === n=2 offsets is not a delay distribution and must not be quoted as one; what is established is that the offset is large and nonzero, not its size. ROUTE TO: session_01TASYv35o6XciFnMC9wmnHi, which is already investigating exactly this question and should own both the OI clearing and the corrected wording — clearing a monitoring row is an observation its clearer must have made, and that session will have the fuller picture including the 02:20Z slot.

items.title: The nightly fleet replay dies on a dropped SSH pipe and reports it as a JSON parse error
items.note: FOUND while sweeping scheduled runs; nobody was looking at it. `replay-pregate-nightly` run #4365 (id 33491178494), event=schedule, 2026-09-01T09:14:38Z, conclusion FAILURE — the ONLY non-success among 30 scheduled runs in the window. It is the sole scheduled failure, so this is a specific break rather than a repo-wide outage. === WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, from the job log: it SSHes the trainer VM and replays a 22-model fleet. Models 1-9 all graded TRUSTWORTHY_SIGNAL (auc 0.7075-0.9487, n 15,816-30,023) — so the driver works and the models are fine. At model 10 of 22 (btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2) the log reads `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, immediately followed by `##[error]no JSON object in driver output`. THE SSH SESSION DROPPED MID-RUN. Plausibly the trainer VM under load — it is 1 OCPU / 6 GB and runs the ML lifecycle — but that is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and nobody has checked. === ⚠️ THE SECOND FINDING IS THE ONE WORTH THE ROW, and it is a textbook instance of a class this repo has already named: `no JSON object in driver output` reports a PARSING failure for what was a CONNECTION failure. A reader is sent to inspect the driver's output format when the pipe broke. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A — 'a failure message that names a cause no code path tested' — which CLAUDE.md documents and `diagnostic-provenance-guard` exists to catch. The fix is to branch on the actual failure STAGE (ssh transport vs driver output) rather than reword the label. === NOT FILED TO A BACKLOG YET, deliberately: this belongs in ml-review-backlog.json and backlog drain #2 (session_01BNXj6o) is live on exactly that file right now — filing into it would hand a sibling a merge conflict for no benefit. File it once that drain lands. === Separate, smaller observation from the same read: this workflow has 4,382 runs, of which the 30 most recent are 29 `issues`-triggered SKIPS and this one scheduled failure. It fires on every issue event in a repo that uses issues as its primary relay mechanism. Not harmful, but it makes the run history nearly unreadable and buries exactly this kind of failure.

items.title: Following the board protocol makes the audit louder, which inverts the incentive
items.note: OBSERVED ON THIS SESSION'S OWN PRs, and the demonstration is unusually clean because it was accidental. The scope-overlap audit fired on SIX consecutive manager PRs (#10712 #10713 #10714 #10715 #10716 #10720), every time attributing docs/claude/work/MANAGER-*.json to a broad `docs/claude/work/` START. At 01:42:42Z the manager posted a PRECISE START naming its session id and exactly the three manager-only files it writes — the correct protocol response. THE NEXT AUDIT (#10720) THEN REPORTED **TWO** OVERLAPS INSTEAD OF ONE, the second being that very comment (issuecomment-5503070932), and still headlined it 'touches files ANOTHER session declared'. === THE DEFECT: the audit compares a PR's changed files against every declared path on the board, but never asks WHOSE declaration it matched. A session that declares its scope correctly is therefore flagged AGAINST ITSELF, and the more precisely it declares, the more overlaps it generates. That inverts the incentive the board exists to create: following the protocol makes the alarm louder, and the cheapest way to a quiet audit is to declare nothing. === WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS — this is the desensitized-alarm P1 in miniature, on the exact surface meant to prevent two sessions colliding. Six identical benign firings in ninety minutes is how a real cross-session overlap becomes invisible; the repo has already paid for this once, when 202 of 376 CRITICAL/ERROR rows in one window were a single un-latched alarm that trained the operator past the channel reserved for an unprotected position. === THE FIX IS KNOWABLE AND NARROW: the board comment carries the declaring session id and the PR carries its own head branch and author, so self-attribution is determinable — either suppress a self-match or label it distinctly ('you declared this') rather than as another session. ⚠️ DO NOT 'fix' it by widening what counts as benign or by removing the audit: it is correct about the overlap and explicitly says it is an observation, not a block. The bug is only in WHO it says declared the path. === Also worth keeping: the audit states its own coverage gap honestly ('This list is a LOWER BOUND' for prose declarations it could not resolve to paths), which is the collapsed-state discipline done right and should survive any fix.

items.title: A better explanation for the never-traded legs than 'long-horizon'
items.blocked_on: operator — the remedy is a Tier-3 disposition or a netted-symbol arbitration policy
items.note: ⚠️ MORNING REPORT. Found by backlog drain #3 (session_01JXBmVC) and it LANDS ON A NUMBER PHASE G MEASURED HOURS EARLIER AND COULD NOT EXPLAIN. Phase G: 12 of 52 enabled legs have never closed a trade, only 11 of 52 would EVER be gradeable at the n>=20 floor; its candidate explanation was 'retire them, or accept they are long-horizon'. Drain #3 supplies a third and better one. === MEASURED, population stated: over a 30.9-day overlap window (2026-08-02T02:27:21Z -> 2026-09-02T00:40:22Z, 805 order packages / 508 closed trades — the window where BOTH diag tables are complete under their 1000-row cap), there were 352 unfilled decisions, ALL attributed, ZERO residual. 163 were `all_accounts_noop`, of which 106 `flip_suppressed_hold_policy` and 56 `hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative` — both DELIBERATE POLICY. Then the deciding test: 141 of 163 (86.5%) were raised while a position in that (account_id, symbol) was ALREADY OPEN, and in every named pairing THE HOLDER IS A DIFFERENT STRATEGY LEG. So a low fill rate on these legs is not lost opportunity — it is a second leg correctly denied a symbol another leg already owns. === THE SHARPEST CASE, filed as PB-20260902-MGC-TREND-1H-IS-LIVE-AND-STRUCTURALLY-CANNOT-TRADE: `mgc_trend_1h` is execution:live and enabled:true with 95 decisions, ZERO fills, ZERO closed trades since 2026-07-26. 55 of 55 of its suppressions were raised while MGC was already open on ib_paper, held ALWAYS by a sibling (ict_scalp_mgc_15m 48, mgc_pullback_1d 7) and NEVER by itself, because it has never held a position. Union-of-intervals occupancy of (ib_paper, MGC) is 73.3%. Three legs share one netted position on one account WITH NO ARBITRATION BEYOND FIRST-COME — which leg trades MGC is decided by arrival order rather than any policy anyone chose. === WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A DEAD LEG: a leg cannot accrue the evidence its own kill-gate demands if a sibling owns the symbol 73% of the time. The M7 gate is therefore not merely under-powered (MI-06) — it is grading legs that were never given the chance to trade. === ⚠️ TWO LIMITS I AM NOT CROSSING. (a) This is a DIFFERENT AXIS from ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE, which arbitrates one symbol across ACCOUNTS; this is contention among legs on the SAME account and symbol. Do not conflate them when fixing. (b) 'Structurally cannot trade' is established for mgc_trend_1h on 95 decisions with zero residual; whether it GENERALISES to the other 11 never-closed legs is UNMEASURED and must not be carried as if it were.

items.title: 17.2% of closed rows store a stop on the wrong side of entry; expectancyR reaches +206.9
items.note: ⚠️ MORNING REPORT. PB-20260821-R-AND-DOLLARS-DISAGREE-IN-SIGN was REFUSED by drain #3 rather than closed, and the refusal is the right call — its criteria split, the real-money limb PASSES (n=28, +$18.40, +44.840R, rCoverage 1.000) and the plausible-bound limb FAILS HARD. Closing on the limb that passed would be exactly the sign-flip-by-choice-of-population failure this repo has already paid for. === THE ROW GOT WORSE, and its mechanism is now proven rather than inferred: it reasoned from ONE trade (4824) that trades.stop_loss holds the CURRENT TRAILED stop rather than the initial one. Direct test over closed rows with pnl NOT NULL (n=477): 82 carry a stored stop on the WRONG SIDE OF ENTRY — impossible for an initial stop — i.e. 17.2%, against the row's n=1. Sign disagreement has spread from 2 of 31 strategy x account_class rows to 7 of 40. Worst: ict_scalp_sol_15m paper n=18, totalPnl -$2,064.01 against totalR +3,724.567. New worst expectancyR +206.920, 59x the one on file, from a SINGLE trade at R = +3,672.32. === WHY IT IS A PRIORITY RATHER THAN A TIDY-UP: it contaminates every totalR / expectancyR consumer, INCLUDING R-BASED PROMOTION GATES. A gate reading expectancyR on this data is reading a number that can exceed its true value by two orders of magnitude. === Needs its own session and the fix is Tier-3 — it changes what a promotion gate reads, which is why a drain session correctly would not write it. === Context worth carrying beside any dollar figure from this fleet: measured fleet pnlCoverage (MEASURED-only via classify_pnl) is 0.126 — 64 of 508 closed trades in that 30.9d window. 87% of the fleet's PnL is not a measurement.

items.title: The trainer relay is issue-driven, and a sub-session's issue_write is 403
items.note: REPORTED BY backlog drain #2 (session_01BNXj6o) as a bound on two of its own refusals, and it is a real CAPABILITY GAP rather than that session's limitation. The trainer VM has NO HTTP diag API — CLAUDE.md is explicit that it is reachable only through the `trainer-vm-diag` ISSUE relay (label trainer-vm-diag-request, body carrying a `cmd:` block). But a sub-session's `issue_write` returns 403 `Resource not accessible by integration` — a write-scope boundary, NOT the transient hosted-MCP drop, so retrying with backoff will never clear it. And the file-drop relays that exist (.github/workflows/pr-opener.yml, board-post.yml) cover PRs and coordination-board posts and NOTHING ELSE. So there is no diag path to the trainer for any sub-session. === WHAT IT COST, concretely: drain #2 could not read dataset_audit.jsonl or training_cycle.jsonl, which is exactly the evidence two of its three refusals needed, and it said so rather than inferring. Its whole stale-shard mechanism is therefore code-plus-live-registry inference — strongly corroborated (identical sibling manifests differing only in dataset.version; all four freezing on the same day; each pinning a low version) but NOT the direct read, and the direct read is one `ls` away for whoever holds that access. === ⚠️ IT ALSO FOUND A PARTIAL WORKAROUND NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN: /api/bot/ml/registry is a live trainer-evidence surface reachable over plain HTTPS with no issue relay, carrying mirror_age_seconds, and it used that successfully (96 rows, HTTP 200, mirror 21.5s old; sibling paths /api/bot/ml/models and /api/bot/models both 404, so the 200 is a real route and not a catch-all). docs/claude/diag-relay.md does not mention it and currently tells such a session the trainer is reachable ONLY via the issue relay — the relay it cannot use. THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE pr-opener / board-post GAP THIS FILE ALREADY RECORDS: a capability that exists and is unreachable from the surface its user reads is, for that user, identical to no capability. The manager told drain #2 to FILE the docs gap rather than fix it in a backlog-drain PR. === ⚠️ NOTE THE PARTIAL: the mirror is a READ of what the trainer published, not a shell on the trainer. It does not cover the jsonl reads that were actually needed, so it narrows this gap without closing it.

items.title: A sub-session's 'I'll stay available' is a hand-off nothing can act on
items.note: MEASURED TWICE TONIGHT, and the second time it cost a real hand-off. The merge-train sub-session (session_01CKcZFm) ended its turn IDLE at 01:46:45Z with post_turn_summary 'staying available to re-resolve as manager merges' — an explicit offer to be re-invoked. When two of its PRs needed exactly that re-resolve, the manager tried `SendMessage` to it and got: **'No agent named session_01CKcZFm... is reachable. Use ListAgents to see everyone you can message.'** `ListAgents` lists only in-process agents and local sessions; a CCR cloud sub-session appears in NEITHER direction. === SO 'STAYING AVAILABLE' IS A DEAD END THAT READS AS A HAND-OFF. That session was holding full context on two conflicted PRs — which files, which resolution rule, what it had already tried — and NONE of it was reachable. The manager had to spawn a fresh session (session_015oCrkh) and re-supply everything it already knew. It worked, but the duplicated context is the cost, and the operator has said that cost is acceptable — which is not the same as it being invisible. === ⚠️ THIS IS THE COORDINATION LIMIT THE OPERATING-MODEL DESIGN ALREADY NAMES, observed live: 'a session that dies cannot run its own close-out', so state must be written to the WORK OBJECT as work happens rather than held in a session that expects to be woken. An IDLE session is the same case as a dead one for this purpose — the design's three mechanisms (incremental progress, a lease per session, a reaper) are the answer, and none of them is 'message it again'. === TWO THINGS A FUTURE MANAGER SHOULD DO DIFFERENTLY: (1) never write a spawn prompt that invites a session to idle and await follow-up — tell it to finish, write its state down, and stop; (2) do not read `post_turn_summary: staying available` as an owner. It is not one. The row is `queued` rather than filed to a backlog because the fix is a change to how sessions are SPAWNED and how hand-off state is RECORDED, which is operating-model work, not a bug in a file.
